title: Galaxy Unpacked D-1: What to Watch as Samsung Unveils New Foldables and AI Gear
description: Samsung Electronics Co. is revamping its foldable smartphone lineup with a wider display and a new top-tier model, betting that hardware innovation will spur demand even as soaring memory costs threaten to push up consumer prices. At its Galaxy Unpacked event in London on July 22, the South Korean tech giant is set to introduce the Galaxy Z Fold 8 series, headlined by a new "Ultra" tier. Breaking away from the traditional narrower design, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra shifts to a wider 4:3 aspect ratio by expanding its width and reducing height. The flagship device will be powered by Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8.5 Gen processor—the same chip featured in the Galaxy S26—and will incorporate a 50-megapixel ultra-wide camera, addressing long-standing criticisms regarding foldable camera performance. Samsung is also introducing "Flex Titanium," a dual-layer structure combining a titanium alloy film and plate designed to minimize screen creases while maintaining structural durability. Notably, however, the privacy display seen on the S26 Ultra will not make the jump to the new foldables. The rollout comes amid mounting cost pressures across the consumer electronics sector. Market researcher Gartner estimates that DRAM and SSD prices could surge by up to 130% by the end of the year, potentially driving smartphone prices up by roughly 13%. Samsung mobile head TM Roh has previously warned that the unprecedented shortage of memory chips will inevitably create pricing headwinds for the industry. In addition to the Z Fold 8 and Z Flip 8, Samsung is accelerating its push into new hardware categories. The company will showcase its AI Glasses, a device first previewed in May that was built in collaboration with Google and runs on Android XR and Gemini. As Samsung introduces new AI form factors—including its smartwatches and the Galaxy Ring—the upcoming event will test whether the tech giant can successfully anchor these devices in the mainstream market. Rounding out the hardware ecosystem, Samsung will also debut the Galaxy Watch 9 and Watch Ultra 2. The new wearables feature optimized internal architecture and improved battery life, alongside advanced health-monitoring tools that analyze sleep metrics, heart rate variability, and skin temperature to generate comprehensive heart health scores and personalized workout recovery advice. sunone@chosunbiz.com
